weeks.title: Q1:W5 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to solve two-step word problems involving multiplication and division, and assess the reasonableness of answers.
sc: I can use the strip diagram to solve two-step problems.
I can write a related multiplication and division equation using a letter or symbol.
I can explain how finding the missing unknown number can help with related facts.

days.lo: I am learning to solve word problems involving time intervals within 1 hour by counting backward and forward using the number line and clock.
sc: I can count forward and backward using a number line to solve word problems involving time intervals within 1 hour.
I can count forward and backward using a clock to solve word problems involving time intervals within 1 hour.

days.lo: I am learning to solve word problems involving time intervals within 1 hour by adding and subtracting on the number line.
sc: I can identify the known start time, end time, or elapsed minutes in a word problem.
I can draw and label a number line to show time intervals precisely.
I can add or subtract intervals of minutes to solve for an unknown time.

days.lo: I am learning to solve addition and subtraction word problems involving time intervals greater than 1 hour.
sc: I can use a clock to find elapsed time.
I can use a number line to find elapsed time.

weeks.title: Q1:W6 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to build and decompose a kilogram with appropriate measurements about the same size and weight of 1 kilogram, 100 grams, 10 grams, and 1 gram.
sc: I can use a pan balance and square units to build and evenly partition a 1-kilogram whole.
I can skip-count by hundreds to show that 1 kilogram is equal to 1,000 grams.
I can identify and label the abbreviations kg and g for different metric weights.

days.lo: I am learning to determine when to use estimation strategies by reasoning about the weight in kilograms of a series of familiar objects to establish mental benchmark measures.
sc: I can hold a 1-kilogram weight to build a mental benchmark of how heavy it feels.
I can use a spring scale or a digital scale to measure and compare my estimated weights.
I can choose the correct unit of metric weight (grams or kilograms) for different objects.

days.lo: I am learning to build and decompose a kilogram to reason about the relationship between the size and weight of kilograms and grams.
sc: I can use unit weights to build up to a total of 1 kilogram.
I can mathematically decompose 1 kilogram into ten 100-gram segments.
I can visually explain how the physical size of an object does not always dictate its metric weight.

days.lo: I am learning to decompose a liter to determine the appropriate size of 1 liter, 100 milliliters, 10 milliliters, and 1 milliliter.
sc: I can explain the relationship between a liter and a milliliter by decomposing units of capacity.
I can create and use a horizontal number line to represent intervals of liquid volume.
I can estimate and measure liquid volume to the nearest 100 milliliters.
days.note: Lessons combined (L8 Concept Development Problem, revised with horizontal number lines)

days.lo: I am learning to decompose a liter to determine the appropriate size of 1 liter, 100 milliliters, 10 milliliters, and 1 milliliter.
sc: I can explain the relationship between a liter and a milliliter by decomposing units of capacity.
I can create and use a horizontal number line to represent intervals of liquid volume.
I can estimate and measure liquid volume to the nearest 100 milliliters.

weeks.title: Q1:W7 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to solve mixed word problems involving all four operations with grams, kilograms, liters, and milliliters given in the same units.
sc: I can solve word problems involving addition and subtraction.
I can solve for the unknown in word problems involving multiplication and division.

days.lo: I am learning to name numbers up to 100,000 by building an understanding of the place value chart and placement of commas for naming base thousand units.
sc: I can build the place value chart from ones to hundred thousands.
I can represent numbers to 100,000 on the place value chart using the chip model.
I can write and say numbers in standard form.
I  can add to make 10 of a unit and bundle up to 1 hundred thousand.

days.lo: I am learning to read and write numbers up to 100,000 using base ten numerals, number names, expanded form, and expanded notation.
sc: I can write up to a five-digit number in word form, expanded form, and expanded notation.
I can transcribe a number in word form to standard form, expanded form, and expanded notation.
I can convert a number in expanded form to expanded notation, word form, and standard form.

days.lo: I am learning to compare numbers based on the meaning of the digits using <, >, or = to record the comparison.
sc: I can compare two numbers with the same largest place value unit.
I can compare two numbers with equal amounts of the largest units.
I can compare values of multiple numbers using a place value chart.
I can compare numbers in different number representations.

weeks.title: Q1:W8 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to round two- and three-digit numbers to the nearest ten on the horizontal number line.
sc: I can tell if a number is more or less than halfway, and use that to decide which ten it rounds to.
I can find the halfway points on a number line between two tens.

days.lo: I am learning to round to the nearest hundred on the horizontal number line.
sc: I can use a horizontal number line to round three-digit numbers to the nearest hundred.
I can use a horizontal number line to  round four-digit numbers to the nearest hundred.

days.lo: I am learning to add measurements using the standard algorithm to compose numbers twice.
sc: I can use place value to understand adding on a horizontal number line.
I can use place value charts, disks, and the standard algorithm to add measurements, composing larger units twice.
I can use multiple strategies and the standard algorithm to add measurements, composing larger units twice.

days.lo: I am learning to estimate sums by rounding and to solve measurement word problems.
sc: I can estimate the sums by rounding.
I can analyze the rounded sums of three expressions with addends close to the halfway point.
I can check the reasonableness of my precise answer by comparing it to my estimated sum.

days.lo: I am learning to decompose once to subtract measurements including three-digit minuends with zeros in the tens or ones place.
sc: I can use the place value chart to model decomposing once to subtract with three-digit minuends.
I can subtract using the standard algorithm.

weeks.title: Q1:W9 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to decompose twice to subtract measurements including three-digit minuends with zeros in the tens and ones places.
sc: I can decompose twice using the standard algorithm for subtraction.
I can use the standard algorithm to subtract three-digit numbers with zeros in various positions.

weeks.title: Q2:W1 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 25-26

days.lo: I will estimate solutions to addition and subtraction problems using rounding.
sc: I can round measurements to the nearest ten or hundred to estimate a difference.
I can calculate the exact difference and evaluate the reasonableness of my estimate.

days.lo: I am learning to use multiplication to compare quantities.
sc: I can draw and label strip diagrams to represent multiplicative comparison problems.
I can write a matching multiplication or division equation to solve for the unknown quantity.
I can describe relationships between quantities using the phrase "times as much" or "times as long".

days.lo: I am learning to use tables to record multiplicative relationships.
sc: I can find the rule of an additive table.
I can find the rule of a multiplicative table.
I can determine the input or output of a table using “times as many as”.

days.lo: I am learning to solve multiplicative comparison word problems.
sc: I can solve multiplicative problems using a strip diagram.
I can write multiplication or division equations using a symbol or box for the unknown.
I can write a solution sentence that directly answers the word problem.

weeks.title: Q2:W2 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to study properties of commutativity to find unknown facts of 6, 7, 8, and 9.
sc: I can explore commutativity as it relates to multiplication.
I can use the multiplication chart to find unknown facts through commutativity.
I can explain how switching the order of factors does not change the product.

days.lo: I am learning to apply the distributive and commutative properties to relate multiplication facts 5 x n + n to 6 x n and n x 6 where n is the size of the unit.
sc: I can use pictures to understand distributive property.
I can add one more group to a known 5s fact to solve an unknown 6s fact.
I can use commutativity to write the related multiplication fact.

days.lo: I am learning to multiply and divide with familiar facts using a box to represent the unknown.
sc: I can use a box to represent the unknown in multiplication.
I can use a box to represent the unknown in division.

days.lo: I am learning to represent skip counting  by units of 6 and 7 to multiply and divide using number bondsto decompose.
sc: I can use number bonds to decompose and make ten as a strategy for skip-counting units of 6 and 7.
I can write skip-counting sequences for 6s and 7s to solve multiplication and division problems.
I can use skip-count by seven to solve multiplication and division problems.

days.lo: I am learning to interpret the unknown in multiplication and division to model and solve problems using units of 6 and 7.
sc: I can draw and label strip diagrams to represent word problems with units of 6 and 7.
I can write multiplication and division equations using a box to represent the unknown.
